speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: asked the Minister for Education (a) whether there are updated figures on local representation in academia in universities; (b) how successful have the Singapore Teaching and Academic Research Talent Scheme, the NUS President's Assistant Professor Scheme and the NTU Nanyang Assistant Professorship Scheme been; (c) how much has been invested in these schemes; and (d) what have been the benefits and key impact of these schemes and the views of faculty about these schemes.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The Ministry of Education (MOE) started the Singapore Teaching and Academic Research Talent (START) Scheme to develop Singaporean academics and to supplement existing schemes at the various AUs.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: As it is relatively new, most of the scholarship recipients are still studying.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Of the 16 who have completed their studies, 13 are holding faculty positions in our AUs, with the rest returning to join the AUs later this year.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: START recipients have already demonstrated involvement in impactful, locally-relevant projects in areas, such as language and palliative care.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The National University of Singapore (NUS) Presidential Young Professorship (PYP) Scheme and the Nanyang Technological University's (NTU’s) Nanyang Assistant Professorship (NAP) Scheme aim to attract top local and foreign academics to the AUs.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Thus far, NUS and NTU have granted a total of 91 awards.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Together, the three schemes provide various forms of support for aspiring and young academics at different stages of their studies and careers.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This comes in the form of financing support during Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) or post-doctorate stints, mentorship from faculty members and research grants.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will continue to work with our AUs to build a strong Singaporean Core in our faculty.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It is critically important that we have a strong core of local academics in our AUs.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: I have spoken on this topic in previous sessions.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: In stating that there is about 50% of local representation in our universities, I would like to ask the Minister whether there are any particular faculties where stints are under-represented in terms of the local academics in these faculties.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: First, in terms of universities, are there certain schools which are lacking?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: And then, within the universities, are there certain faculties where the number of local academics is lacking?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: If so, what are the measures that will be taken to boost these numbers?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: When it comes to Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM), by nature, the research and teaching are international.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: In fact, the more international inputs you have, the richer the experience in terms of student learning as well as the richer the research outcomes.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, my short answer is, that will be our focus.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We are actively discussing with the autonomous AUs, not just now, but for the past year or two.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: PYP, NAP and START are such schemes that could help build up arts and social sciences' local faculties in these areas.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But there are also other practical steps that we are discussing with all our AUs and we will implement them in time to come.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: The first is whether the Minister could share more on the age profile of Singapore versus foreign faculty.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: This is because, anecdotally, it seems that many Singapore faculty are concentrated in the older side of the profession because they pre-date our opening up of the sector to foreign faculty.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: The second supplementary question is if the Minister could share more on the academic ranks and positions held by Singapore versus foreign faculty because there is a difference between holding a tenure track or tenured position, and holding, for example, a teaching position which is much less secure and is less flexible.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The age profile of faculty, I am afraid, I do not have those data with me.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: If the Member would file a Parliamentary Question, we are happy to answer.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: How is it that we have 50% local academics over the past 10 years?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Because we do watch those data and make sure that it is not just the stock that matters but also the flow, which is why we need a START scheme so that we bring in young local academics from young.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I would not say it is particularly skewed.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Fifty percent applies to the whole academic faculty as well as tenured positions.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As Members know, it is also important for us, especially in comprehensive universities like NUS and NTU, that we do not just focus on the tenured professorships.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: It is also very, very important to recognise that the primary mission of our AUs is actually to educate the young and develop them.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, teaching and practice professorships are, in fact, very important, too.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And I really hope to see – and that is one point that Mr Seah Kian Peng asked – that we can elevate teaching professorships to be really on par with tenured research professorships.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Speaker, I declare my interest as a faculty member in a local AU.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Is there an over-emphasis on publication, academic research and university ranking that we compromise the quality of teaching amongst our faculty?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Anecdotally, again, when a particular university wanted to chase university rankings, a lot of foreign faculty members were brought in based on their past publication of research and not so much on the quality of teaching, which then has an impact on our students.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: First of all, we should be clear high ranking is not bad.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Actually, to be ranked high internationally is something we should be proud that NUS and NTU have all been ranked high.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: If you ask most universities or most governments whether they wish to have a university that ranks high, whether it is Quacquarelli Symonds or Times Higher Education, they will say, "I wish we have NUS and NTU".

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We are very well aware of that in the Ministry Headquarters and so are the leaders of our AUs.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: [Pursuant to Standing Order No 22(3), provided that Members had not asked for questions standing in their names to be postponed to a later Sitting day or withdrawn, written answers to questions not reached by the end of Question Time are reproduced in the Appendix.]
